rows.how: Inside the published range: 150 µm plus the P2 width in a laser-scribed perovskite mini-module, 180 µm in 156 cm² modules.
Module TCOs are limited to about 7 to 60 Ω per square; a commercial FTO glass is sold at 7 Ω per square.
A cost study allows about 1 cm of edge seal around the glass. On the 0.6 × 1.2 m module of the reference line that is 4.9% of the area, so 3% is optimistic; Note S9 tests 0% and 6%.

rows.how: Same loss split (geometric loss of the P1-P2-P3 dead area, resistive loss in the TCO) and the same R·J·w²/(3V) form.

SIMsalabim default (1E20 m⁻³ = 10¹⁴ cm⁻³); a review gives about 10¹⁴ cm⁻³ or lower as the threshold for high-performance films.

rows.item: Trap density scenarios (base times or divided by √10)
rows.how: The span 3.2E19 to 3.2E20 m⁻³ lies inside values fitted to working perovskite cells (below 1.1E19 up to 2.0E21 m⁻³).

SIMsalabim default (1E-4 m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ = 1 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹). Long-range mobilities measured in MAPbI₃ and mixed perovskite films are 0.3 to 6.7 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, but as a sum of electron and hole mobilities, so a single carrier has about half (0.15 to 3.4 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹).

rows.item: Mobility scenarios (base times or divided by √10)
rows.how: 0.32 to 3.2 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ for the electron mobility, inside the single-carrier range of about 0.15 to 3.4 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ implied by the measured sum of mobilities.

rows.item: Ideal contacts: infinite surface recombination, no series resistance, infinite shunt
rows.how: SIMsalabim default contact setting; another open perovskite drift-diffusion code also uses Ohmic contacts. With no contact or resistive losses, efficiencies are upper bounds.

rows.item: Band edges: C₆₀ E_c 4.0, PTAA E_v 5.4, SnO₂ E_c 4.0, NiOx E_v 5.7 eV
rows.how: C₆₀ and PTAA are SIMsalabim default layers; SnO₂ and NiOx come from the electron affinity and band gap in a published device table.

rows.item: No regional adjustment of the Chinese capital cost
rows.how: PV manufacturing in China is 10% cheaper than in India, 20% than in the United States and 35% than in Europe, with investment cost among the drivers; module making in ASEAN costs about 5% more than in China, mainly through overhead and labour. The Chinese figure therefore probably understates cost in Malaysia.

rows.how: World Bank lending rate. The cost of equity is generally above the cost of debt (a bank loan), so the true cost of capital is higher.

rows.item: Process electricity per step (sputtering, printing, annealing)
rows.how: Step inventory of a perovskite/silicon tandem life-cycle study, priced at the Malaysian tariff.

rows.item: Maintenance, share of capital per year
rows.how: 1% is used by two perovskite cost studies; a roll-to-roll study uses 4% for building and facility maintenance, so 1% is probably low. Note S9 tests 3% and 7%.

rows.item: Omitted overheads: land, rent, facilities, cleanroom and HVAC base load
rows.how: Bottom-up perovskite module models count facility rent and utilities as overhead, so leaving them out makes O a lower bound.

rows.how: Official Malaysian rates for wages of RM5,000 and below. The effect on O is computed in this note.

rows.item: Hole-side interlayer for n-i-p Cu/Ag (post-hoc bound, Note S16): 10 nm MoO₃
rows.how: 10 nm evaporated MoO₃ under Cu or Ag is used in published perovskite cells. Bulk molybdic oxide costs 51 USD/kg (2025e); density 4.69 g/cm³; step electricity proxied by the Cu evaporation step. A lower estimate: evaporation-grade powder, tool capital and time are excluded.
